title: RAW UNREVIEWED: oko as a solar body and oko-aiin as its fixed-zodiac return interval
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. In the complete existing f68r2 rings and f89v1 paragraph, distinguish a body from an interval derived from that body: ok=MOON, oko=SUN; one aiin constructor returns the first complete proper circuit in an explicitly fixed zodiac frame. Exact okaiin and okoaiin then carry different body arguments without two independent whole-period glosses. Upper-ring bare oko is a new solar-participant obligation, not the Moon label. No first-word meaning, chody predicate, numeral or complete clause is filled in.

target.scope_limit: 58 ring groups and230 prose groups; no new outside loci, texts, images or target queries. The three readers are not independent witnesses.

base_atoms.ok: MOON as a celestial body; this is a newly guessed stem value, not an identified free ok occurrence in these units
base_atoms.oko: SUN as a celestial body, both as exact bare group and as exact licensed compound host

new_meanings_and_writer.constructor: aiin: CelestialBody -> ProperReturnIntervalSpec. Apply exactly the same operation to ok and oko, with no distinct Moon/Sun wholeword interval entries.
new_meanings_and_writer.fixed_reference_frame: F is the source-style zodiac circle for the body's proper west-to-east motion, not the daily carried east-to-west firmament motion. Fix one common marked starting longitude lambda0 and its first positive complete proper return. F and lambda0 are common background parameters, unbound to a target glyph and openly paid; they cannot switch by token, register or desired duration.
new_meanings_and_writer.output_type: An interval specification: (body,F,lambda0,first_positive_complete_return). It is neither the body, one currently observed event, a calendar date, a magnitude, daylight, nor a patient material. A specific occurrence/start epoch or numeric duration would need an additional written/contextual binding, not supplied here.
new_meanings_and_writer.bare_core_identity: The same oko core denotes SUN in a bare group and inside okoaiin. Exact prefix overlap is not by itself evidence of that identity; it is a new declared compositional assumption.
new_meanings_and_writer.scope: Only these two bases and two exact compound licenses are assigned. No global aiin=PERIOD, no inherited three, no deletion of internal o, no new d/q/ch/r/ar/or/y meanings.
new_meanings_and_writer.first_ring_groups: okeo,okey,ekey remain unassigned. In particular ZL/RF lower ring repeats okey atG1 andG8/G7; IT has firstokeo but laterekey. Any later constructor must preserve each exact reuse and every variant; this card assigns no separate convenient sense at the inner occurrence.
new_meanings_and_writer.other_forms: okor and okar remain unresolved whole forms, including ZL ok[a:?]r. GDT062 and GDT605 disagree about their cuts; no Moon translation of their whole forms is obtained merely from proposed ok. okol is not reduced to oko+l or assigned SUNLIGHT; qokaiin/chokaiin retain q/ch and are not silently equal to okaiin. The known inner ok|aiin analysis is recorded but outer wrapper meanings remain missing.

actual_written_applications.consequence: The Moon-associated ring would refer to the Sun somewhere in its complete account. The body owning the picture is not automatically the denotation of every ring group.
A proper solar-course interval spec, not the Sun body or mineral gold; no numeric year is supplied.
A subsequent complete prose construction must use that temporal type with the same frame; SUN actor, GOLD patient, DAYLIGHT or a one-day interval cannot be substituted here.
The second actual written host instantiates the same constructor. The two interval specs retain distinct body arguments; no equality of their lengths or phases is asserted.

additional_written_consequences: The exact upper-ring bareoko and lower-ring okoaiin share SUN as base under the rule but differ in type. Thus the upper ring contains a solar participant while the lower has a derived solar interval; this is a new conditional cross-ring obligation beyond simply naming the two pictures.

The same f89v1 paragraph contains solar and lunar return interval forms under one aiin rule. Any later fixed reading that needs literal Sun for okoaiin but a plain material for okaiin violates this contract; it cannot repair this by a per-token frame or suffix switch.

A solar return in the fixed proper-zodiac frame includes recurrent daily visible and invisible phases. It cannot become a daytime-only exposure window simply because the prose is pharmaceutical. No written number, end marker or illumination instruction is identified in the current units.

All exact bareoko appearances in a prospectively retained outside complete context would have the literal SUN-body value under an unchanged extension. A known outside okar oko bigram alone does not bind its relation or translate okar.

rivals.name: Visibility interval constructor
rivals.difference: Would map a body to an interval determined by an observer/site, local horizon and visibility criterion. These are additional fixed arguments, not the zodiac return frame. A genuine visible interval can terminate while the body continues its course; lunar visibility need not mean NIGHT. This is a conceptual rival only; no alternate rule is allowed to replace W's fixed return operation at an inconvenient position.
